items.prompt: How confident are you that you could name the five jobs a model can do inside a product and say when plain code is the better choice?
A feature listens to a voicemail and produces text the app can use. Which model job is that?

options.label: Perceive — turning messy human information into something software can use
Act — performing an operation in the world

items.explanation: Transcribing speech is perceive work: understanding input traditional software struggles with, not acting or deciding.

items.prompt: Take one app idea you have. Write one feature that needs AI and say which job it is — perceive, interpret, generate, decide or act — plus one feature that should stay plain code.

criteria: Names a feature and matches it to a sensible model job
Names a rule-like feature and keeps it as normal code

items.prompt: In your own words, explain the difference between asking an AI to decide and asking code to decide.

criteria: Explains that AI suits ambiguous interpretation while code suits fixed rules
Gives one example of each or explains why reliable rules should stay code

items.prompt: How confident are you that you could explain who performs an action when an AI agent uses a tool?
An agent sends a refund by calling a refund tool. Who actually performs the refund?

options.label: The model, by writing the refund sentence
Application code executing the tool the model requested

items.explanation: The model chooses or requests the action; the surrounding application performs the real operation.

items.prompt: Invent one tool for a school-club agent — for example get_schedule or send_reminder. Write its name, what input it needs, and what it returns to the model.

criteria: Defines a concrete tool with a clear name and purpose
Specifies a sensible input and what the application returns to the model

items.prompt: In your own words, explain why the model chose the action and the application performed the action can both be true at once.

criteria: Separates deciding or requesting from executing
Mentions that developers define the tools and their input and output shapes

items.prompt: How confident are you that you could choose the lowest rung of AI architecture that still solves a problem?
A feature takes one messy paragraph and must return five structured fields. What is the simplest sufficient design?

options.label: A single model call that returns the fields
An autonomous agent with a tool loop

items.explanation: One input and one structured output need no loop and no autonomy; more agents would only add cost, latency and debugging difficulty.

items.prompt: Take one feature idea and place it on the ladder: model call, grounded AI, AI workflow or agent. Write one sentence defending your level.

criteria: Picks a plausible ladder level for the stated feature
Justifies the choice by simplicity or by who controls the steps

items.prompt: In your own words, explain the difference between an AI workflow and an agent.

criteria: States that workflow steps are predetermined while an agent chooses its next step
Notes that the agent's flexibility makes it harder to control and test

items.prompt: How confident are you that you could explain why more AI autonomy requires more limits and verification?
An agent can search, read, draft, send and delete. Which actions should require human approval?

options.label: None of them — agents are meant to be autonomous

items.explanation: AI saying something wrong and doing something wrong are different risk levels; consequential actions deserve confirmation.

items.prompt: Write two stopping conditions you would give an agent that researches scholarship deadlines — for example limits on searches, minutes, cost or retries.

criteria: Gives two concrete limits such as tool calls, time, cost or retries
Frames them as architecture the system enforces, not suggestions to the model

items.prompt: In your own words, explain why an agent without stopping rules is unfinished software rather than more autonomous.

criteria: Explains that unlimited loops can burn cost and time without finishing
Connects autonomy to needing more verification and control around it
